title: ‘Broken Promises’—Ten Hag Breaks Silence on Ronaldo, Kane & Man Utd Chaos
subtitle: SI
paragraphs: By Tom Gott6:55 AM EDTErik ten Hag’s Man Utd tenure was a rollercoaster. / Martin Rickett/PA Images/Getty Images, Matthew Ashton - AMA/Getty Images, James Gill - Danehouse/Getty Images, Uwe Anspach/picture alliance/Getty Images, Alex Dodd - CameraSport/Getty ImagesErik ten Hag arrived at Manchester United in the summer of 2022 as one of the most exciting young managers around, given the unenviable task of fixing a team whose decline had been nothing short of extraordinary.

His two years at the helm were anything but simple. The Dutchman won two trophies, fought with Cristiano Ronaldo and watched over some of the worst signings in club history. So, when he sat down with The Athletic to pull back the curtain on his tenure, it came as no surprise that he had plenty to say.
Here are five key takeaways from the interview.

Ten Hag was not happy with the direction of the club. / John Walton/PA Images/Getty ImagesTen Hag’s departure from United was a comedy, the sort of which you would pay to see in the theater.

An infamous end-of-season review into his position saw United speak with a handful of big-name alternatives before not only persisting with Ten Hag, but offering him a new contract. Three months later, he was fired.

“I wouldn’t go on with only one year left,” Ten Hag reflected. “So I said, ‘I need an extra year and we have to do it together.’ They promised me loyalty, they promised me backing, they promised communication, that we get aligned. We spoke about the issues. But the promises, they didn’t keep.”
Among the biggest broken promises to Ten Hag was the sale of homegrown midfielder Scott McTominay.

Only Bruno Fernandes and Rasmus Højlund scored more goals for United in 2023–24 than the Scotland international, who Ten Hag claims he was assured would remain at Old Trafford just weeks before he was flipped to Napoli.
“That’s why I got disappointed,” the manager explained. “In Ibiza, we agreed. I said, ‘No selling Scott McTominay.’ We would go aligned in the transfer window.

“I make an argument, a reason: we don’t have scoring abilities. Scott brings scoring abilities and great mentality. He has United in all his veins. So when they bring up the subject, ‘No.’ And in the end they sold him. I got, of course, very embarrassed and disappointed.”

Raphaël Varane (left) and Casemiro (right) both swapped Real Madrid for Man Utd. / Martin Rickett/PA Images/Getty ImagesIn April 2022, as the club waited for Ten Hag to join, interim boss Ralf Rangnick argued United needed “open heart surgery” as he insisted everybody at Old Trafford had to get on the same page and address a culture of toxicity that had been allowed to breed.

The very same issue Rangnick tried to warn against reared its ugly head during Ten Hag’s reign and played a key part in the tenure of his successor, Ruben Amorim. There is even a case to suggest it is still alive and kicking to this day.
According to Ten Hag, United are responsible for allowing this culture to continue.
“They are continuing the toxic culture; they fuel it, they give the power to the players.”
“Players have to act, they have a big responsibility. Football is, for some, not the highest priority. And United for some wasn’t the highest priority.”

Ten Hag then touched on what he described as the “Madrid connection,” referencing a series of signing of former Real Madrid stars. Raphaël Varane and Cristiano Ronaldo were already at United when Ten Hag joined and Casemiro followed the pair over in the summer of 2022.
The Dutchman accused the trio of contributing to the issues at United with egos built from years of playing at the highest level.
“I can say I think that’s what the Madrid connection brought in, that players are powerful and they want to decide,” he said. “In my opinion it didn’t suit the phase United was in.
“The leadership wanted attacking, dynamic football and these players wanted to play what fitted themselves.”
